title: Like all the nations (1 Samuel 8)
hookLine: the people ask for a king like everyone else, and Samuel warns them

cards: The elders of Israel gather at Samuel's home in Ramah, and they put it plainly. Samuel has judged Israel for a lifetime, going round a circuit from town to town, and he has made his sons judges after him.
It hasn't worked. His sons, the text says, did not walk in his ways. They turned aside after gain, took bribes, and bent justice.
So: you are old, and your sons don't walk in your ways. Now make us a king to judge us, like all the nations.

teach.b: Their complaint is fair; the text says so before they do. But listen to the last phrase. Not just, give us a better judge.
Like all the nations. They want to look like everyone around them. The thing displeases Samuel, and he prays.
Listen to the people, God tells him: they have not rejected you, but they have rejected Me, that I should not be king over them. Still, give them what they ask. But warn them first.
So Samuel tells them what a king will do. He will take your sons for his chariots and his horsemen, to plow his ground and reap his harvest and make his weapons.
He will take your daughters to be perfumers, cooks and bakers. He'll take your best fields and vineyards for his servants, and a tenth of your grain and your flocks.
Take, and take, and take. And you'll be his servants, and you'll cry out on that day because of the king you chose.

teach.h: WE WILL HAVE A KING ANYWAY.
teach.b: The people answer: no; but we will have a king over us, that we also may be like all the nations, that our king may judge us, and go out before us, and fight our battles. They've heard the cost, and they still want it.
God tells Samuel: listen to their voice, and make them a king. Some readers hear a warning about power here.

teach.h: THAT WE ALSO MAY BE LIKE ALL THE NATIONS.
teach.b: Others hear how badly people can want to be like everyone else.

how: Jewish commentators differ on this chapter: some read the request for a king as wrong in itself, others read Deuteronomy as allowing a king and fault only the people's motive, to be like the nations.

games.why: Samuel warns them: he will take your sons, your daughters, your fields, a tenth of your flocks. they hear it all, and still say: we will have a king.

practice: Bring to mind one thing you've been wanting lately, a phone, a job title, a kind of life, and ask Samuel's question gently: what will it take from me?
Then ask the elders' question honestly: do I want it because it's good, or because everyone around me has one?

wordCard.voice: king. What the elders of Israel ask Samuel for, to be like everyone around them, even after he warns them what it will take.

carryVoice: Your line: take, and take, and take. A fair complaint can carry another wish inside it. Day seven hundred thirty-one.
